---
title: Lightbox Figures
lightbox: true
---

## Overview

A lightbox lets a reader click an image to see a larger version of it on
top of the page, with its caption. Images can also be grouped into a
gallery, so the reader can page through them without going back to the
document. Quarto uses the [GLightbox](https://biati-digital.github.io/glightbox/)
library for this in HTML pages.

This page uses `lightbox: true`, so the image below opens in a lightbox
when you click it:

![An elephant](../../authoring/elephant.png){width=50%}

## Enabling lightbox

To give every image in a document the lightbox treatment, set `lightbox`
to `true` (or `auto`, which means the same) in the front matter, or under
`format: html:`, or in `_quarto.yml` for the whole project:

``` yaml
---
title: Simple Lightbox Example
lightbox: true
---

![A Lovely Image](mv-1.jpg)
```

In this automatic mode, Quarto picks every figure and every image that
sits alone in its own paragraph. Images that appear inline, within a line
of text, are left alone.

### Applying lightbox to specific images

To give the treatment to selected images only, leave `lightbox` unset and
add the `lightbox` class to those images. There is no need to set anything
in the front matter:

``` markdown
![A Lovely Image](mv-1.jpg){.lightbox}

![Another Lovely Image](mv-2.jpg)
```

Here the first image gets a lightbox and the second does not. The class
also works on inline images, which automatic mode skips.

## Disabling lightbox

To turn lightbox off for a whole document, even for images that carry the
`lightbox` class:

``` yaml
---
lightbox: false
---
```

### Disabling lightbox for specific images

In automatic mode, give an image the `nolightbox` class to leave it out:

``` markdown
---
lightbox: auto
---

![A Lovely Image](mv-1.jpg)

![Another Lovely Image](mv-2.jpg){.nolightbox}
```

Images that are already links, like `[![A ferry](ferry.png)](https://example.com)`,
never get a lightbox: clicking them follows the link.

## Galleries

Give images the same `group` attribute to put them in one gallery. When
the reader opens one of them, they can page through the others:

``` markdown
![A Lovely Image](mv-1.jpg){group="my-gallery"}

![Another Lovely Image](mv-2.jpg){group="my-gallery"}

![The Last Lovely Image](mv-3.jpg){group="my-gallery"}
```

Without a `group`, each image is a gallery of its own.

## Options

Instead of `true`, `lightbox` can be a set of options:

| Option          | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| `match`         | Set to `auto` to give every image the lightbox treatment. If you leave it out, only images with the `lightbox` class get it. |
| `effect`        | The effect used to open and close the lightbox: `fade`, `zoom` or `none`. Defaults to `zoom`. |
| `desc-position` | Where the title and description go: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. Defaults to `bottom`. |
| `loop`          | Whether paging past the last image of a gallery goes back to the first. Defaults to `false`. |
| `css-class`     | A class name for the lightbox, for targeting it with your own CSS. It replaces GLightbox's own skin class. |

A complete example:

``` yaml
---
title: Complete Lightbox Example
lightbox:
  match: auto
  effect: fade
  desc-position: right
  loop: false
  css-class: "my-css-class"
---
```

An invalid value produces a warning and the option's default is used.

## Per-image attributes

These attributes can be set on individual images:

| Attribute       | Description |
|-----------------|-------------|
| `group`         | The gallery the image belongs to. |
| `description`   | Text shown below the title in the lightbox. It is Markdown, so it can contain emphasis, links and so on. |
| `desc-position` | Where this image's title and description go: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`. |
| `title`         | The title shown in the lightbox, instead of the caption. |

For example:

``` markdown
![Beach in Chilmark](mv-0.jpg){description="Some of the best beaches on the island. _Credit:_ [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com)" desc-position="left"}
```

The title shown in the lightbox is the image's caption. For a figure you
can cross-reference, it includes the figure number, as in "Figure 1:
A Lovely Image". An image without a caption uses its alt text.

## Using lightbox with computational cells

Plots produced by code cells are figures, so in automatic mode they get the
lightbox treatment like any other figure, including the figure number when
they have a label:

```` markdown
---
lightbox: auto
---

```{r}
#| label: fig-basic
#| fig-cap: Simple demo R plot
plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
```
````

A cell can also pass options through its `lightbox` option. Use `false` to
leave the cell's plots out, or a set of attributes to apply to them. When a
cell makes several plots, give a list to set a different value for each:

```` markdown
```{r}
#| fig-cap:
#|   - Caption for first plot
#|   - Caption for second plot
#| lightbox:
#|   group: cars
#|   description:
#|     - This is the description for the first graph
#|     - This is the description for the second graph
plot(mtcars)
plot(cars)
```
````

## The `quarto-ext/lightbox` extension

Lightbox used to be provided by the `quarto-ext/lightbox` extension. It is
now built in, so a document that still lists that extension under
`filters` gets a warning, the entry is ignored, and the built-in lightbox
is used. Remove the entry and the extension's `_extensions/quarto-ext/lightbox/`
folder.

## Differences from Quarto 1

- Lightbox works in HTML documents and websites. Reveal.js presentations
  and dashboards don't support it yet.
- `q2 preview` doesn't open the lightbox. The images still show, and
  clicking them does nothing. `q2 render` gives the full behaviour.
- The cell `lightbox` option works with the knitr engine. With the
  Jupyter engine it is not passed on yet.
- Subfigures (`fig-subcap`) are not supported yet, so the subfigures of a
  figure don't form a gallery of their own yet.
- An invalid option value is a warning, not an error, and `loop` is
  documented with the default it has always had, `false`.
